calculation_steps: Expand published U1[2cos(ky y)cos(kx x)+cos(2ky y)] into three equal-amplitude cosines with |g|=4pi sqrt(N)/(sqrt(3)a).
Solve each eta qdot_j+kappa q_j=lambda U1 cos(g_j.(r0+vt)) and average velocity-odd force; obtain F_d=-C sum g_j(g_j.v)/(1+tau²(g_j.v)²).
Use exact dyad sum=3g²I/2 for low-speed isotropic tensor.
For directional cosines at 0 and 30 degrees, compute exact S2=3/2, S4=9/8 and S6=33/32 versus 27/32, giving first cos6phi term at z^4 in normalized power.
Square Table4 rounded U1 magnitudes and multiply by g7²/g13²=7/13 to obtain 651175/6877; compare separately with scalar-cut 4.33 under inequivalent transfer assumptions.
Differentiate low-speed coefficient in pressure; full response retains finite-speed z dependence.

counterexamples_and_failures: Earlier 4.33 scalar-cut surrogate and this 94.69 first-star null use inequivalent physical coupling maps; static data do not identify which maps to measured friction.
At finite speed the ratio depends on angle, slide direction and g v tau, so 94.69 is not universal.
Unknown mode mixing or unequal losses can alter high-speed angular response; C3-preserving symmetric linear tensor stays isotropic but scalar changes.
limitations: No measured loss/contact/pressure derivatives or force threshold; source PRL full text unavailable.
PES Table4 rigid coefficients have opposite signs and finite fit deviations; ratio is from rounded theoretical values.
Assumed equal independent baths and per-atom contact transfer are not UD-native.
Stationary modes may produce conservative transverse forces at fixed initial registry, excluded from dissipative phase-averaged expression.
No independent physics review or physical promotion.
changed_dependencies: Refines the earlier 1D conventional null by using the published full first-star geometry and exposes transfer-map identifiability.
